title: CTET — Combined: Language II English + Language I Hindi
description: Combined test: Language II English + Language I Hindi for CTET. 40Q.
subject: ctet-language2
instructions: Subject: Language II English + Language I Hindi

questions.question: Which of the following is the *primary* purpose of developing listening skills in a language classroom?

options.text: To enable students to reproduce sounds accurately.
options.explanation: Reproducing sounds is more related to pronunciation skills rather than listening comprehension.

options.text: To help students understand and interpret spoken messages.
options.explanation: This is the core purpose of developing listening skills.

options.text: To improve students' ability to memorize vocabulary.
options.explanation: Memorizing vocabulary is a separate skill, though listening can aid in vocabulary acquisition.

options.text: To prepare students for oral examinations.
options.explanation: Oral examinations are a specific context, not the primary purpose of listening skills.

questions.explanation: The primary goal of listening comprehension is to decode, understand, and interpret meaning from spoken language. While other options might be secondary benefits, understanding and interpretation are central to comprehension.
questions.hint: Focus on the core objective of listening skills in language learning.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A teacher plays an audio story and asks students to identify the main characters, setting, and plot sequence. This activity primarily aims to develop which aspect of listening?

options.text: Listening for specific details.
options.explanation: This activity goes beyond just identifying specific details.

options.text: Listening for gist/main idea.
options.explanation: The activity focuses on understanding the overall narrative components.

options.text: Inferential listening.
options.explanation: Inferential listening involves drawing conclusions, which is not the primary focus here.

options.text: Critical listening.
options.explanation: Critical listening involves evaluating the content, which is not the main goal of this activity.

questions.explanation: Identifying main characters, setting, and plot sequence requires students to grasp the overall understanding or the main idea of the story, rather than focusing on isolated specific details.
questions.hint: Consider whether the activity focuses on overall understanding or specific details.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A Grade VI teacher notices that her students struggle to understand spoken English when the speaker uses a fast pace or unfamiliar accents, even when the vocabulary is known. What would be the *most effective* long-term strategy to address this specific challenge?

options.text: Provide transcripts of all audio materials for students to read along.
options.explanation: Reading along may help with understanding but does not train the ear for speed or accent.

options.text: Expose students to a wide variety of authentic audio materials with different paces and accents.
options.explanation: This directly addresses the challenge by building familiarity and adaptability.

options.text: Focus solely on slow-paced, clear audio from textbooks until proficiency is achieved.
options.explanation: This approach does not prepare students for real-world listening situations.

options.text: Ask students to repeat sentences after the teacher to improve pronunciation.
options.explanation: This focuses on speaking rather than listening comprehension for varied input.

questions.explanation: Exposing students to diverse authentic input directly addresses the core problem by building familiarity and adaptability with different paces and accents.
questions.hint: Consider long-term strategies that build familiarity and adaptability.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: When a listener is actively paying attention to a speaker, showing interest, and providing verbal or non-verbal feedback, they are demonstrating:

options.text: Passive listening.
options.explanation: Passive listening involves minimal engagement and no feedback.

options.text: Selective listening.
options.explanation: Selective listening involves focusing only on certain parts of the message.

options.text: Active listening.
options.explanation: Active listening involves full engagement and feedback.

options.text: Critical listening.
options.explanation: Critical listening involves evaluating the content, not just engagement.

questions.explanation: Active listening involves full engagement with the speaker, including showing interest and providing feedback.
questions.hint: Consider the level of engagement and feedback in the listening process.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: Which of the following is *not* a barrier to effective listening in a classroom?

options.text: Preconceived notions about the topic or speaker.
options.explanation: Preconceived notions can hinder effective listening.

options.text: Physical distractions like noise or poor acoustics.
options.explanation: Physical distractions can hinder effective listening.

options.text: Lack of interest or motivation in the listener.
options.explanation: Lack of interest can hinder effective listening.

options.text: The teacher providing clear instructions and scaffolding.
options.explanation: Clear instructions and scaffolding facilitate effective listening.

questions.explanation: Clear instructions and scaffolding are supportive teaching practices that facilitate learning and listening, rather than acting as barriers.
questions.hint: Identify which option does not hinder effective listening.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A teacher uses a recorded news bulletin in the classroom and asks students to identify the speaker's tone, purpose, and potential bias. This activity encourages:

options.text: Intensive listening.
options.explanation: Intensive listening focuses on understanding factual content, not evaluation.

options.text: Extensive listening.
options.explanation: Extensive listening focuses on overall understanding or pleasure, not evaluation.

options.text: Critical listening.
options.explanation: Critical listening involves evaluating and analyzing the message.

options.text: Appreciative listening.
options.explanation: Appreciative listening focuses on enjoyment, not evaluation.

questions.explanation: Identifying tone, purpose, and bias involves evaluating, analyzing, and forming judgments about the message, which are hallmarks of critical listening.
questions.hint: Consider the level of analysis and evaluation required in the activity.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: To develop listening comprehension for young learners, a teacher should primarily focus on:

options.text: Exposing them to complex grammatical structures through audio.
options.explanation: Complex grammar is too advanced for initial listening development.

options.text: Providing simple, repetitive, and context-rich audio materials.
options.explanation: This is effective for building listening comprehension in young learners.

options.text: Requiring them to transcribe long audio passages.
options.explanation: Transcription is too advanced and not effective for initial development.

options.text: Asking them to memorize dialogues from audio clips.
options.explanation: Memorization is less effective than context-rich input for comprehension.

questions.explanation: For young learners, simple, repetitive, and context-rich input is crucial for language acquisition and building listening comprehension.
questions.hint: Consider the developmental needs of young learners in language acquisition.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: Which activity would be *least effective* for improving listening comprehension in a communicative language teaching (CLT) classroom?

options.text: Students listening to a conversation and identifying the speakers' opinions.
options.explanation: This activity is communicative and focuses on understanding meaning.

options.text: Students listening to a weather report and drawing symbols for the forecast.
options.explanation: This activity is communicative and focuses on understanding meaning.

options.text: Students listening to a lecture and taking detailed notes on every word.
options.explanation: This activity is rote and detracts from meaningful communication.

options.text: Students listening to a podcast and summarizing the main points for a partner.
options.explanation: This activity is communicative and focuses on understanding meaning.

questions.explanation: Taking detailed notes on *every word* is often rote, can be overwhelming, and may detract from understanding the overall message or engaging with the content for communication.
questions.hint: Consider the principles of communicative language teaching and the focus on meaningful communication.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A teacher plays an audio recording of a short dialogue and then asks students to answer specific questions about factual information mentioned in the dialogue (e.g., 'What time did the train leave?'). This type of listening is known as:

options.text: Listening for pleasure.
options.explanation: This activity is not focused on pleasure.

options.text: Listening for gist.
options.explanation: This activity focuses on specific details, not the overall understanding.

options.text: Listening for specific information.
options.explanation: This activity focuses on specific factual details.

options.text: Listening for inference.
options.explanation: This activity does not focus on drawing conclusions.

questions.explanation: Asking for precise factual details directly targets the skill of listening for specific information.
questions.hint: Consider whether the activity focuses on overall understanding or specific details.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: According to Krashen's Input Hypothesis, effective listening comprehension for language acquisition occurs when learners are exposed to:

options.text: Input that is significantly above their current level of competence (i + 10).
options.explanation: Input that is too far above their level is less effective for acquisition.

options.text: Input that is slightly beyond their current level of competence (i + 1).
options.explanation: This is the core principle of Krashen's Input Hypothesis.

options.text: Input that is exactly at their current level of competence (i).
options.explanation: Input at their current level does not push acquisition forward.

options.text: Input that is below their current level of competence (i - 1).
options.explanation: Input below their level does not challenge them to acquire new language.

questions.explanation: Krashen's Input Hypothesis states that language acquisition occurs when learners are exposed to 'comprehensible input' that is slightly above their current level of competence (i + 1).
questions.hint: Consider Krashen's theory on language acquisition and the role of input.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of developing listening skills in a language learner?

options.text: To enable them to produce grammatically correct sentences.
options.explanation: This relates to speaking or writing, not the primary purpose of listening.

options.text: To help them master the art of public speaking.
options.explanation: Public speaking is a productive skill, not the goal of listening.

options.text: To comprehend spoken messages and acquire language input for overall proficiency.
options.explanation: This is the core purpose of listening as a receptive skill.

options.text: To improve their ability to write essays and reports.
options.explanation: Writing is a separate productive skill, not the goal of listening.

questions.explanation: The primary purpose of listening is comprehension of spoken language, which is fundamental for receiving language input and subsequently developing other language skills like speaking, reading, and writing. Options A, B, and D relate to productive or other receptive skills, not the core purpose of listening itself.
questions.hint: Focus on the core function of listening as a receptive skill.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT typically considered a sub-skill of effective listening comprehension?

options.text: Inferring meaning from context.
options.explanation: This is a key sub-skill of listening comprehension.

options.text: Identifying the main idea and supporting details.
options.explanation: This is a fundamental sub-skill of listening comprehension.

options.text: Producing grammatically correct spoken responses.
options.explanation: This is a sub-skill of speaking, not listening.

options.text: Understanding intonation and stress patterns.
options.explanation: This is a sub-skill of listening comprehension.

questions.explanation: Producing grammatically correct spoken responses (C) is a sub-skill of speaking, a productive skill. The other options (A, B, D) are all integral sub-skills of listening comprehension, which involves understanding and interpreting spoken language.
questions.hint: Identify which option relates to a productive skill rather than a receptive one.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A teacher plays an audio story and asks students to sequence the events in chronological order. This activity primarily assesses students' ability to:

options.text: Infer the speaker's mood and tone.
options.explanation: This is a higher-order listening skill but not the primary focus of sequencing.

options.text: Understand specific details and their sequential relationship.
options.explanation: This is the core skill being assessed in sequencing events.

options.text: Identify the main theme or moral of the story.
options.explanation: This is a different listening skill, not directly related to sequencing.

options.text: Recognize different regional accents.
options.explanation: This is unrelated to the task of sequencing events.

questions.explanation: Sequencing events requires students to accurately grasp specific pieces of information and understand the order in which they occurred. While other listening skills might be incidentally used, the primary focus is on detailed comprehension and chronological understanding.
questions.hint: Consider what skill is most directly tested by sequencing events.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: To promote 'top-down' listening in the classroom, a teacher should encourage students to:

options.text: Focus meticulously on individual words and grammar structures.
options.explanation: This is 'bottom-up' processing, not top-down.

options.text: Use their background knowledge and contextual clues to understand the overall message.
options.explanation: This is the essence of top-down listening.

options.text: Repeatedly listen to the same audio segment until every word is understood.
options.explanation: This is 'bottom-up' processing, focusing on details.

options.text: Transcribe the audio word-for-word to ensure accuracy.
options.explanation: This is 'bottom-up' processing, not top-down.

questions.explanation: Top-down listening involves using prior knowledge, context, and expectations to understand the gist or overall meaning, moving from the general to the specific. Options A, C, and D describe 'bottom-up' processing, which focuses on decoding individual linguistic units.
questions.hint: Top-down listening relies on background knowledge and context.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A student frequently asks for repetitions when listening to instructions, even for simple tasks. This suggests a potential difficulty primarily in:

options.text: Extensive listening.
options.explanation: This involves understanding longer texts, not basic instructions.

options.text: Discriminative listening.
options.explanation: This skill involves distinguishing sounds and words, which is likely the student's challenge.

options.text: Inferential listening.
options.explanation: This involves understanding implied meaning, not basic instructions.

options.text: Appreciative listening.
options.explanation: This involves enjoying or appreciating spoken language, not understanding instructions.

questions.explanation: Discriminative listening (B) involves distinguishing between sounds, words, and phrases, which is crucial for understanding basic instructions. If a student constantly needs repetition, they might be struggling to clearly discriminate the spoken input. Extensive listening is for general understanding of longer texts, inferential for implied meaning, and appreciative for enjoyment.
questions.hint: Consider which type of listening skill involves distinguishing sounds and words.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: In a multilingual classroom, a teacher introduces a listening task where students listen to a short audio clip and then collaboratively summarize it in their own words. This approach primarily aims to:

options.text: Minimize the use of the mother tongue in the classroom.
options.explanation: The task does not explicitly aim to minimize mother tongue use.

options.text: Develop critical thinking and collaborative communication skills alongside listening comprehension.
options.explanation: This is the primary aim of the collaborative summarization task.

options.text: Exclusively assess individual listening comprehension without peer support.
options.explanation: The task involves peer collaboration, not individual assessment.

options.text: Ensure all students achieve native-like pronunciation.
options.explanation: Pronunciation is not the focus of this task.

questions.explanation: Collaborative summarization (B) goes beyond mere listening. It encourages students to process information critically, negotiate meaning with peers, and express their understanding, thus integrating listening with critical thinking and speaking/communication skills. It leverages the multilingual environment for peer learning rather than minimizing mother tongue (A) or focusing on individual assessment (C) or pronunciation (D).
questions.hint: Consider the broader skills developed through collaborative tasks.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate pre-listening activity for a news report about a recent natural disaster?

options.text: Asking students to write a summary of the report before listening.
options.explanation: This is impossible as students have not yet heard the report.

options.text: Discussing related vocabulary and students' prior knowledge about natural disasters.
options.explanation: This is a classic pre-listening activity to build schema and introduce key terms.

options.text: Immediately playing the audio and asking comprehension questions.
options.explanation: This is a listening activity, not a pre-listening one.

options.text: Asking students to translate the report into their mother tongue.
options.explanation: Translation is a post-listening or analytical task, not preparatory.

questions.explanation: Pre-listening activities (B) are designed to activate schema, build background knowledge, and introduce key vocabulary, making the listening task more accessible and effective. Writing a summary before listening (A) is impossible. Playing immediately (C) can be overwhelming. Translation (D) is a post-listening or analytical task, not preparatory.
questions.hint: Pre-listening activities should prepare students for the topic and vocabulary.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A teacher wants to develop students' ability to listen for gist and main ideas from a longer, authentic audio source. Which of the following activities would be LEAST effective for this specific goal?

options.text: Asking students to identify the speaker's purpose after listening.
options.explanation: This encourages understanding of the main message.

options.text: Having students complete a multiple-choice quiz on overall themes.
options.explanation: This focuses on the main ideas and themes.

options.text: Requiring students to write down every unfamiliar word they hear.
options.explanation: This promotes attention to detail, which is counterproductive for gist comprehension.

options.text: Asking students to choose the best title for the audio clip.
options.explanation: This focuses on the main idea or gist of the audio.

questions.explanation: Listening for gist and main ideas requires a holistic understanding, not a focus on every detail. Requiring students to write down every unfamiliar word (C) promotes 'bottom-up' processing and attention to detail, which can hinder their ability to grasp the overall message. Options A, B, and D all encourage understanding of the main message or purpose.
questions.hint: Consider which activity focuses too much on details rather than the overall message.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: When teaching listening skills, 'scaffolding' primarily refers to:

options.text: Providing increasingly difficult listening tasks without any support.
options.explanation: This describes progression but not scaffolding.

options.text: Offering support and guidance that is gradually withdrawn as learners become more proficient.
options.explanation: This is the definition of scaffolding in teaching.

options.text: Focusing solely on native speaker accents and fast speech from the beginning.
options.explanation: This is not related to scaffolding.

options.text: Using only audio-visual aids for all listening activities regardless of learner level.
options.explanation: This is not the definition of scaffolding.

questions.explanation: Scaffolding (B) is a pedagogical approach where teachers provide temporary support to learners, helping them achieve a task they couldn't do independently, and then gradually removing that support as the learner's competence grows. This aligns with Vygotsky's Zone of Proximal Development.
questions.hint: Scaffolding involves temporary support that is gradually removed.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: A Grade 5 teacher notices that despite repeated exposure to English audio, some students struggle with inferring meaning from context during listening tasks. Which strategy would be most effective in addressing this specific challenge?

options.text: Providing transcripts and asking students to read along while listening.
options.explanation: This may improve decoding but does not directly target inferential skills.

options.text: Focusing on explicit grammar rules related to sentence structure.
options.explanation: Grammar rules do not directly help with inferring meaning from context.

options.text: Engaging students in discussions about cultural nuances and speaker's implied intentions in short, targeted audio clips.
options.explanation: This directly addresses inferential listening by focusing on implied meanings and cultural context.

options.text: Increasing the speed of the audio to challenge their processing ability.
options.explanation: This may overwhelm students and does not directly address inferential skills.

questions.explanation: Inferring meaning (C) goes beyond explicit information and involves understanding implied messages, speaker's attitudes, and cultural context. Engaging in discussions about these aspects directly targets the development of inferential skills. Reading along (A) might improve decoding but not necessarily inference. Grammar rules (B) are not.
questions.hint: Consider which strategy directly addresses the skill of inferring meaning.
questions.subject: ctet-language2

questions.question: भाषा अधिग्रहण और भाषा अधिगम के बीच मुख्य अंतर क्या है?

options.text: भाषा अधिग्रहण चेतन प्रक्रिया है जबकि भाषा अधिगम अचेतन।
options.explanation: यह कथन गलत है क्योंकि भाषा अधिग्रहण अचेतन होता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम चेतन।

options.text: भाषा अधिग्रहण स्वाभाविक और अचेतन प्रक्रिया है जबकि भाषा अधिगम सचेत और प्रयासपूर्ण।
options.explanation: यह कथन सही है और दोनों प्रक्रियाओं के बीच मुख्य अंतर को स्पष्ट करता है।

options.text: भाषा अधिग्रहण केवल औपचारिक कक्षाओं में होता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम घर पर।
options.explanation: यह कथन गलत है क्योंकि भाषा अधिग्रहण घर पर स्वाभाविक रूप से होता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम औपचारिक कक्षाओं में।

options.text: भाषा अधिग्रहण में व्याकरण के नियमों पर जोर दिया जाता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम में नहीं।
options.explanation: यह कथन गलत है क्योंकि भाषा अधिग्रहण में व्याकरण के नियमों पर जोर नहीं दिया जाता जबकि भाषा अधिगम में जोर दिया जाता है।

questions.explanation: भाषा अधिग्रहण (Language Acquisition) एक स्वाभाविक, अचेतन प्रक्रिया है जिसमें बच्चा बिना किसी औपचारिक निर्देश के अपनी मातृभाषा सीखता है। वहीं, भाषा अधिगम (Language Learning) एक सचेत, प्रयासपूर्ण प्रक्रिया है जिसमें नियमों और संरचनाओं पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया जाता है, अक्सर औपचारिक कक्षाओं में।
questions.hint: भाषा अधिग्रहण स्वाभाविक होता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम प्रयासपूर्ण।
questions.subject: ctet-language1

questions.question: भाषा अर्जन और भाषा अधिगम के संदर्भ में, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही नहीं है?

options.text: भाषा अर्जन एक स्वाभाविक प्रक्रिया है, जबकि भाषा अधिगम प्रयासपूर्ण होता है।
options.explanation: यह कथन सही है क्योंकि भाषा अर्जन स्वाभाविक होता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम प्रयासपूर्ण होता है।

options.text: भाषा अर्जन में प्रायः विद्यालयी शिक्षा की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।
options.explanation: यह कथन सही है क्योंकि भाषा अर्जन में विद्यालयी शिक्षा की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।

options.text: भाषा अधिगम में व्याकरणिक नियमों पर बल दिया जाता है।
options.explanation: यह कथन सही है क्योंकि भाषा अधिगम में व्याकरणिक नियमों पर बल दिया जाता है।

options.text: भाषा अर्जन में बच्चे को नियम सिखाए जाते हैं, जबकि भाषा अधिगम में बच्चा नियम स्वतः सीखता है।
options.explanation: यह कथन गलत है क्योंकि भाषा अर्जन में बच्चा नियम स्वतः सीखता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम में नियम सिखाए जाते हैं।

questions.explanation: विकल्प D गलत है। भाषा अर्जन में बच्चा नियम स्वतः (अचेतन रूप से) सीखता है और यह एक स्वाभाविक प्रक्रिया है। भाषा अधिगम में प्रायः नियमों को सिखाया जाता है या उन पर ध्यान केंद्रित किया जाता है। विकल्प A, B और C भाषा अर्जन और अधिगम के बारे में सही कथन हैं।
questions.hint: भाषा अर्जन स्वाभाविक होता है जबकि भाषा अधिगम प्रयासपूर्ण।
questions.subject: ctet-language1

questions.question: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन 'भाषा अधिग्रहण' (Language Acquisition) के संबंध में सही है?

options.text: यह एक सचेत और प्रयासपूर्ण प्रक्रिया है।
options.explanation: यह भाषा सीखने (Language Learning) के लिए सही है, अधिग्रहण के लिए नहीं।

options.text: इसमें व्याकरण के नियमों को रटना शामिल है।
options.explanation: भाषा अधिग्रहण में व्याकरण के नियमों को रटने की आवश्यकता नहीं होती।

options.text: यह एक स्वाभाविक और अचेतन प्रक्रिया है।
options.explanation: भाषा अधिग्रहण एक स्वाभाविक और अचेतन प्रक्रिया है।

options.text: यह केवल औपचारिक विद्यालयी शिक्षा के माध्यम से होता है।
options.explanation: भाषा अधिग्रहण औपचारिक शिक्षा के बिना भी होता है।

questions.explanation: भाषा के विकास के लिए एक समृद्ध भाषाई वातावरण जहाँ बच्चा स्वाभाविक रूप से भाषा सुन सके, बोल सके और उसका प्रयोग कर सके, सबसे महत्वपूर्ण है।
questions.hint: बच्चे को भाषा सीखने के लिए अर्थपूर्ण संदर्भों की आवश्यकता होती है।
questions.subject: ctet-language1

questions.question: एक बच्चा अपनी मातृभाषा को बिना किसी औपचारिक निर्देश के सहजता से सीख लेता है। यह किस प्रक्रिया का उदाहरण है?

options.text: भाषा अधिगम (Language Learning)
options.explanation: भाषा अधिगम एक सचेत, औपचारिक प्रक्रिया है जो आमतौर पर दूसरी भाषा सीखने में प्रयुक्त होती है।

options.text: भाषा अधिग्रहण (Language Acquisition)
options.explanation: मातृभाषा का स्वाभाविक सीखना भाषा अधिग्रहण का उदाहरण है।

options.text: रटना (Rote Memorization)
options.explanation: रटना भाषा सीखने की एक अस्वाभाविक प्रक्रिया है।

options.text: औपचारिक अनुदेश (Formal Instruction)
options.explanation: औपचारिक अनुदेश के बिना सीखना अधिग्रहण कहलाता है।

questions.explanation: मातृभाषा का सहजता से सीखना भाषा अधिग्रहण (Language Acquisition) कहलाता है। यह एक प्राकृतिक, अवचेतन प्रक्रिया है जो बच्चे को अपने परिवेश से भाषा को बिना किसी औपचारिक प्रयास के आत्मसात करने में मदद करती है।
questions.hint: औपचारिक निर्देश के बिना सीखना अधिग्रहण कहलाता है।
questions.subject: ctet-language1

questions.question: प्राथमिक स्तर पर एक बच्चा भाषा प्रयोग करते समय अक्सर व्याकरणिक त्रुटियाँ करता है। एक शिक्षक के रूप में आप इस स्थिति को कैसे देखेंगे?

options.text: यह बच्चे की भाषा सीखने की क्षमता में कमी का संकेत है।
options.explanation: त्रुटियाँ बच्चे की सीखने की प्रक्रिया का हिस्सा हैं, क्षमता में कमी नहीं।

options.text: त्रुटियाँ भाषा सीखने की प्रक्रिया का एक स्वाभाविक और आवश्यक हिस्सा हैं।
options.explanation: त्रुटियाँ बच्चे के भाषाई विकास का संकेत हैं।

options.text: बच्चे को तुरंत और बार-बार उसकी त्रुटियों को सुधारने के लिए दंडित किया जाना चाहिए।
options.explanation: दंड देने से बच्चे की सीखने की रुचि कम हो सकती है।

options.text: बच्चे को तब तक बोलने से रोका जाना चाहिए जब तक वह सही व्याकरण का प्रयोग न करे।
options.explanation: बच्चे को बोलने से रोकना उसके भाषाई विकास में बाधा उत्पन्न कर सकता है।

questions.explanation: प्राथमिक स्तर पर बच्चों द्वारा की गई व्याकरणिक त्रुटियाँ सीखने की प्रक्रिया का एक स्वाभाविक हिस्सा हैं। ये त्रुटियाँ दर्शाती हैं कि बच्चा भाषा के नियमों को समझने और उनका प्रयोग करने का प्रयास कर रहा है, और ये उसके भाषाई विकास के संकेत हैं।
questions.hint: त्रुटियाँ सीखने का हिस्सा हैं, न कि असफलता का।
questions.subject: ctet-language1

questions.question: भाषा अधिग्रहण को बढ़ावा देने के लिए प्राथमिक विद्यालय के शिक्षकों को अपनी कक्षा में क्या करना चाहिए?

options.text: व्याकरण के नियमों को रटवाने पर अधिक जोर देना चाहिए।
options.explanation: रटने से भाषा अधिग्रहण में बाधा उत्पन्न हो सकती है।

options.text: बच्चों को भाषा के प्रयोग के अधिक से अधिक अवसर प्रदान करने चाहिए।
options.explanation: भाषा के प्रयोग के अवसर बच्चे के भाषाई विकास के लिए आवश्यक हैं।

options.text: केवल पाठ्यपुस्तकों में दिए गए अभ्यासों पर ध्यान केंद्रित करना चाहिए।
options.explanation: पाठ्यपुस्तकों तक सीमित रहने से भाषा अधिग्रहण प्रभावित हो सकता है।

options.text: बच्चों को त्रुटियाँ करने से हतोत्साहित करना चाहिए।
options.explanation: त्रुटियाँ सीखने का हिस्सा हैं, उन्हें हतोत्साहित नहीं किया जाना चाहिए।

questions.explanation: भाषा अधिग्रहण को बढ़ावा देने का सबसे प्रभावी तरीका बच्चों को वास्तविक और अर्थपूर्ण संदर्भों में भाषा का प्रयोग करने के भरपूर अवसर प्रदान करना है।
questions.hint: बच्चों को भाषा का प्रयोग करने के लिए प्रोत्साहित करें।
questions.subject: ctet-language1

questions.question: नोम चॉम्स्की के अनुसार, मनुष्य में भाषा सीखने की एक जन्मजात क्षमता होती है। इस क्षमता को क्या कहा जाता है?

options.text: भाषा प्रदर्शन उपकरण (Language Performance Device)
options.explanation: यह चॉम्स्की द्वारा प्रस्तावित अवधारणा नहीं है।

options.text: भाषा इनपुट प्रणाली (Language Input System)
options.explanation: यह चॉम्स्की द्वारा प्रस्तावित अवधारणा नहीं है।

options.text: भाषा अधिग्रहण उपकरण (Language Acquisition Device - LAD)
options.explanation: यह चॉम्स्की द्वारा प्रस्तावित जन्मजात क्षमता का नाम है।

options.text: भाषा अधिगम प्रणाली (Language Learning System)
options.explanation: यह चॉम्स्की द्वारा प्रस्तावित अवधारणा नहीं है।

questions.explanation: नोम चॉम्स्की ने 'भाषा अधिग्रहण उपकरण' (Language Acquisition Device - LAD) की अवधारणा दी, जिसके अनुसार मनुष्य एक जन्मजात, मस्तिष्क-आधारित क्षमता के साथ पैदा होते हैं जो उन्हें भाषा के नियमों को समझने और आत्मसात करने में सक्षम बनाती है।
questions.hint: इस अवधारणा का नाम एक अंग्रेजी शब्दावली से लिया गया है।
questions.subject: ctet-language1

questions.question: एक बच्चा जो 10 साल की उम्र तक मानवीय भाषा के संपर्क से पूरी तरह से अलग रहा है, उसे अब एक समृद्ध भाषाई वातावरण में लाया जाता है। भाषा अधिग्रहण के संबंध में सबसे संभावित परिणाम क्या होगा?

options.text: वह पूरी तरह से और बहुत जल्दी भाषा सीख जाएगा।
options.explanation: 10 साल की उम्र तक भाषा के संपर्क से वंचित रहने के बाद पूर्ण भाषा सीखना कठिन हो जाता है।

options.text: वह बुनियादी भाषा सीख पाएगा, लेकिन महत्वपूर्ण कठिनाइयों के साथ।
options.explanation: पूर्ण देशी-जैसी प्रवीणता प्राप्त करना कठिन हो सकता है, लेकिन बुनियादी भाषा सीखना संभव है।

options.text: वह कभी भी पूर्ण देशी वक्ता जैसी प्रवीणता प्राप्त नहीं कर पाएगा।
options.explanation: महत्वपूर्ण अवधि परिकल्पना के अनुसार, 10 साल की उम्र तक भाषा के संपर्क से वंचित रहने के बाद पूर्ण देशी-जैसी प्रवीणता प्राप्त करना कठिन हो जाता है।

options.text: वह केवल औपचारिक शिक्षण के माध्यम से ही भाषा सीख पाएगा।
options.explanation: औपचारिक शिक्षण के माध्यम से भी पूर्ण देशी-जैसी प्रवीणता प्राप्त करना कठिन हो सकता है।

questions.explanation: यह प्रश्न 'महत्वपूर्ण अवधि परिकल्पना' (Critical Period Hypothesis) पर आधारित है, जो सुझाव देती है कि भाषा अधिग्रहण के लिए एक विशिष्ट विकासात्मक अवधि होती है, जिसके बाद पूर्ण देशी-जैसी प्रवीणता प्राप्त करना बहुत कठिन या असंभव हो जाता है।
questions.hint: भाषा अधिग्रहण की एक निश्चित समय सीमा होती है।
questions.subject: ctet-language1
